issues.failure_explanation: In Case 2 the redefined extension equals f(h,z) on [-λ0 h, λ0 h] and equals f(u,z) for |u| ≥ λ0 h. Since λ0 > 1 and f(λ0 h,z) ≠ f(h,z) in general, this function has jumps at ±λ0 h, which are lattice points jh. The text still treats it as continuous, and Stenger's Poisson theorem needs the mid-value condition at jumps. The overlapping cases leave the value at ±λ0 h ambiguous. The sampled sum h Σ_{|j|≤λ0} f̄(jh) also uses f(h) instead of f(jh) for 2 ≤ |j| ≤ λ0. The closing identity instead writes the plateau term as 2λ0 h f(λ0 h,z), which is inconsistent with the plateau value f(h,z). The relation between the Poisson-summation defect and the quadrature error E_Q is therefore not established as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take the plateau value f(λ0 h,z) so the extension is continuous. Then bound the extra discrepancy h Σ_{2≤|j|≤λ0}[f(λ0 h)-f(jh)] and the mismatched plateau terms by O(T^l e^{-T}) using the existing pointwise bounds on f. Redo the final identity accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform quadrature bound for z with x ≤ x* (near the singularity) is not rigorously derived. Every rate in the paper that rests on the quadrature theorem inherits this gap for those z.
issues.title: Case 2 of the quadrature theorem uses a discontinuous, inconsistent extension to which Poisson summation and the quadrature identity do not apply as written
issues.why_classification: The extra terms are bounded by the same O(T^l e^{-T}) estimates already in the proof, so a local redefinition and bookkeeping fix preserves all stated rates.

issues.failure_explanation: Since (4π²α/h)T = (4π²/σ)√N1, the second term in the braces is about e^{-(4π²/σ)√N1}. This is smaller than e^{-T} = e^{-σα√N1} only when σ ≤ 2π/√α. For σ > 2π/√α (allowed when σ > σ_opt) it is larger, so the equality to O(T^l e^{-T}) is false. The correct target for σ > σ_opt is e^{-η²T}, with η²T = 2π²(2-β)√N1/σ. The T^l factor is placed in front of the whole bracket. For l = 1 and β = 0, where 4π²/σ = η²T/√N1, this leaves T·e^{-η²T}. That contradicts the claimed σ > σ_opt rate with no √N factor for z^α log z, and the pole residues at s_k carry no T^l factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Do not collapse the bracket. Keep the residue-sum term as O(e^{-η²T}) from Lemma residual, without the T^l prefactor. Keep O(T^l e^{-T}) only for the vertical-segment and tail terms. Use T^l e^{-T} = O(e^{-η²T}) when η < 1, and conclude E_Q = O(e^{-η²T}) for σ > σ_opt.
issues.overall_effect: For z near 0 (z outside S_β'), the Case 2 argument does not give the claimed E_Q bound when σ > 2π/√α. For l = 1, β = 0 and σ > σ_opt it gives the wrong rate, which affects the no-√N claim for the logarithmic case and its corollaries.
issues.title: Case 2 Poisson-sum bound collapsed to O(T^l e^{-T}), which fails for large sigma and puts a spurious T^l on the sigma > sigma_opt rate
issues.why_classification: A local re-bookkeeping with estimates already in the paper restores the stated rates; the method, rates and scope are unchanged.
